Access to Biological Collection Data Home

ABCD List of Terms

Title : ABCD List of Terms

Date version issued : 2024-02-28

Date created : 2024-02-28

Part of TDWG Standard : http://www.tdwg.org/standards/115

This version : http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/doc/list/2025-05-25

Latest version : http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/doc/list/

Abstract :The Access to Biological Collections Data (ABCD) Schema is an evolving comprehensive standard for the access to and exchange of data about specimens and observations (a.k.a. primary biodiversity data). The ABCD Schema attempts to be comprehensive and highly structured, supporting data from a wide variety of databases. It is compatible with several existing data standards. Parallel structures exist so that either (or both) atomised data and free-text can be accommodated. Versions 1.2 and 2.06 are currently in use with the GBIF (Global Biodiversity Information Facility, http://www.gbif.org/) and BioCASe (Biological Collection Access Service for Europe, http://www.biocase.org/) networks. Apart from the GBIF and BioCASe networks, the potential for the application of ABCD extends to internal networks, or in-house legacy data access (e.g. datasets from external sources that shall not be converted and integrated into an institution’s own data, but be kept separately, though easily accessible). By defining relations between terms, ABCD is a step towards an ontology for biological collections.

Contributors :

Creator : ABCD Maintence Group

Bibliographic citation : Access to Biological Collections Data Task Group. 2005. Access to Biological Collection Data (ABCD). Biodiversity Information Standards (TDWG) http://www.tdwg.org/standards/115

1.2 RFC 2119 key words

The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

Term Name abcd2:DataSets

Belongs to Group DataSet
Required True
Repeatable False

Label language

However, use of UND is discouraged by the W3 consortium.\n\nRecommended values are defined by the following reference: H. Alvestrand, ed. RFC 3066: Tags for the Identification of Languages 1995. Available at: http://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc3066.txt .\n

Label InheritedName
Definition The inherited name of the data collection owner. This may consist of family names, generational names, a clan name, parents or grandparents personal names, etc. The inherited name (this being the lastname in western cultures) may be compound (e.g. 'Fischer von Waldheim', 'da Selva', 'Silvano Morales'). Depending on culture, the inherited name is not necessarily the name of the parents nor common to a married couple. Therefore, 'family name' should be avoided even though used in vCard (vCard: N-Family).

Term Name abcd2:Unit-Owner-InheritedName
Term IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/Unit-Owner-InheritedName
Label InheritedName
Definition The inherited name of the owner of the unit record. This may consist of family names, generational names, a clan name, parents or grandparents personal names, etc. The inherited name (this being the lastname in western cultures) may be compound (e.g. 'Fischer von Waldheim', 'da Selva', 'Silvano Morales'). Depending on culture, the inherited name is not necessarily the name of the parents nor common to a married couple. Therefore, 'family name' should be avoided even though used in vCard (vCard: N-Family).

Term Name abcd2:UnitContentContact-InheritedName
Term IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/UnitContentContact-InheritedName
Label InheritedName
Definition The inherited name of the administrative contact for the unit record. This may consist of family names, generational names, a clan name, parents or grandparents personal names, etc. The inherited name (this being the lastname in western cultures) may be compound (e.g. 'Fischer von Waldheim', 'da Selva', 'Silvano Morales'). Depending on culture, the inherited name is not necessarily the name of the parents nor common to a married couple. Therefore, 'family name' should be avoided even though used in vCard (vCard: N-Family).

Notes Note that if a higher taxon such as a family name is the result of the identification itself, it should (also) be noted under Full-Scientific-Name-String (mandatory) and Genus-Or-Monomial (optional).

Term Name abcd2:TaxonIdentified-HigherTaxon
Term IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/TaxonIdentified-HigherTaxon
Label HigherTaxon
Definition The scientific name and rank of a taxon with a rank higher than Genus that is used by the data source to classify the taxon name assigned to the unit in the identification event. Although this is not really within the scope of ABCD's data domain, this item is kept for compatibility reasons (Darwin Core) and because for the time being searches are often executed using this item (although classification may vary considerably in source datasets). Eventually, we hope that this function will largely be replaced by taxon and name services defined and provided elsewhere. It is highly recommended to make use of the rank element, because this is a prerequisit for data transformation to Darwin Core.
Notes Note that if a higher taxon such as a family name is the result of the identification itself, it should (also) be noted under Full-Scientific-Name-String (mandatory) and Genus-Or-Monomial (optional).
XPath /DataSets/DataSet/Units/Unit/Identifications/Identification/Result/TaxonIdentified/HigherTaxa/HigherTaxon
Parent TaxonIdentified-HigherTaxa
Belongs to Group Identification
Required True
Repeatable True
Position within Parent 1
RDF Type rdfs:Class
Modified 2005-09-09
Term Version IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/version/TaxonIdentified-HigherTaxon-2005-09-09
Term Name abcd2:TaxonIdentified-HigherTaxonName
Term IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/TaxonIdentified-HigherTaxonName
Label HigherTaxonName
Definition A generic or higher taxon name (monomial) in accordance with rules of nomenclature and associated with the identified taxon. This is not necessarily the result of the identification event, but a classification added to the result of the identification in the source database.
Notes Note that if a higher taxon such as a family name is the result of the identification itself, it should (also) be noted under Full-Scientific-Name-String (mandatory) and Genus-Or-Monomial (optional).
Examples
  • Plantae
  • Acanthaceae
  • Lepidoptera
  • Pisces

Term Name abcd2:TaxonIdentified-HigherTaxonRank
Term IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/TaxonIdentified-HigherTaxonRank
Label HigherTaxonRank
Definition The rank designation of the associated higher taxon (above the rank of genus). The fully spelled out rank value (in latin but for the unranked term and the group levels). This can be used as metadata for any name for a taxon of rank above the genus-level.<br/>It is strongly recommended to use this element, since a rank value is required in order to transform ABCD data for higher taxa to Darwin Core.
Notes Note that this is not the abbreviation for a rank that is used in a botanical infraspecific name, as it appears in the name.

Term Name abcd2:TaxonIdentified-Botanical-GenusOrMonomial
Term IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/TaxonIdentified-Botanical-GenusOrMonomial
Label GenusOrMonomial
Definition One of the following, representing the genus, or higher taxon name, identified for the unit:<br/><br/>A generic name as a botanical scientific name or as part of it <br/><br/>A manuscript name<br/><br/>An intergeneric hybrid name under the ICBN, without the leading multiplication sign <br/><br/>The name of an intergeneric graft hybrid or graft chimaera, published under the Cultivated Code.<br/><br/>Rules: First letter capitalised; No spaces included.
Usage Note that the classification of the identification result (e.g. the family of the species identified) is accommodated by the elements under HigherTaxa.
Notes Generic names are essentially the same under the different codes; however, to avoid having to place the essential parts of a name on different levels of the hierarchy, all name elements recognized under a specific code are listed in the respective section.
Examples
  • Abies
  • Halimiocistus
  • Crataegomespilus
  • Allium

Label InfraspecificEpithet
Definition The final epithet of a botanical name of infraspecific rank identified for the unit.<br/><br/>The infraspecific epithet (i.e. the epithet following the indication of the infraspecific rank in the name string (trinomial)).<br/><br/>Subtaxa can be used to store any additional taxonomic identifier, in latin. Following abbreviations are allowed: subsp. (for subspecies); convar. (for convariety); var. (for variety); f. (for form).<br/><br/>Rules: <br/><br/>1 No uppercase <br/><br/>2. No space
Notes Note that quadrinomials etc. are not supported here as names; if deemed necessary, they can be entered in the FullScientificNameString, this element should than contain the last infraspecific epithet.
Examples
  • subsp. fuscum

Belongs to Group Identification
Required False
Repeatable False

Definition The inherited name of the unit identifier. This may consist of family names, generational names, a clan name, parents or grandparents personal names, etc. The inherited name (this being the lastname in western cultures) may be compound (e.g. 'Fischer von Waldheim', 'da Selva', 'Silvano Morales'). Therefore, 'family name' should be avoided even though used in vCard (vCard: N-Family).

Term Name abcd2:Identification-Date
Term IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/Identification-Date
Label Date
Definition The date of the unit identification event. Identification dates are commonly incompletely known (e.g. only the year or year and month) or unknown. Sometimes identification dates are inferred from a researcher's visit or the duration of a loan.<br/><br/>The rather complex ABCD {{{DateTime}}} type is used, although many of its elements are not normally needed. As a rule, only the {{{IsoDateTimeBegin}}} element is mapped, which is the one used for searches and which can be used to construct identification histories. Alternatively, the {{{DateText}}} element can also be used, but it provides only for human readability. <br/><br/>However, the elements for exact time and periods may be useful for time series in laboratory reports that can be formulated as a series of identification events, or where the result of the identification may be influenced by the duration of a detection process.
XPath /DataSets/DataSet/Units/Unit/Identifications/Identification/Date
Parent Identification
Belongs to Group Identification
Required False
Repeatable False
Position within Parent 8
RDF Type rdfs:Class
Modified 2005-09-09
Term Version IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/version/Identification-Date-2005-09-09
Term Name abcd2:Identification-DateText
Term IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/Identification-DateText
Label DateText
Definition A text version (alphabetic mixed case and integer) of the date at which the unit identification event took place. This element is meant for use when the date is imprecise, ambiguous or not in a form that satisfies the standard structured date format. It can also be used when it is important to record the verbatim representation of the date or when dates to be recorded are not completely legible. For example the day and month may be decipherable but not the year; the use of this field will allow recording of partially interpreted information.<br/><br/>This field can be used to record generalised date ranges and irresolvable ambiguity such as different day/month order conventions (e.g. US/Europe) or to allow for multiple dates and periods.
Notes Note that this element is not normally used for searches.
Examples
  • 25 [?] 1925
  • 3/9/45 [ambiguous day month]
  • Spring 1912
  • Late 1800s
  • End of 19th Century
  • Mid 1978
  • Easter 1933
  • Post WW2
  • Before June 25, 2000
  • After June 25, 2000
XPath /DataSets/DataSet/Units/Unit/Identifications/Identification/Date/DateText
Parent Identification-Date
Belongs to Group Identification
Required False
Repeatable False
Position within Parent 1
RDF Type rdf:Property
Modified 2005-09-09
Term Version IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/version/Identification-DateText-2005-09-09
Term Name abcd2:Identification-TimeZone
Term IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/Identification-TimeZone
Label TimeZone
Definition The time zone to which the time-of-day data for the unit identification event refer. <br/><br/>Timezone expressed in minutes in accordance with the seven property model for date/time attributes in XML schema (http://www.w3.org/TR/2004/WD-xmlschema11-2-20040716/#theSevenPropertyModel). <br/><br/> An integer between -840 and 840 inclusive (+/- 14 hours).
Notes Note that this element is not normally used for identifications.<br/><br/>The time zone to which the time-of-day data for the unit identification event refer.
Examples
  • +570
  • -300

Term Name abcd2:Identification-ISODateTimeBegin

Label ISODateTimeBegin
Definition The exact date (and time) or beginning of a period representing the unit identification event, expressed in a modified ISO/ANSI 8601 standard structured date format.
Usage The date format looks like this: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS with flexible precision.
Notes Note that this is the most commonly used element here. If it is impossible to map (because the db values are not in an ISO string format or the internal db date datatype), one has to use the {{{DateText}}} element (AbcdConcept0383).
Examples
  • 2005-04-10T17:34:56\n2005-04-10T17:34\n2005-04-10T17\n2005-04-10\n2005-04\n2005

Definition The inherited name of the specimen owner. This may consist of family names, generational names, a clan name, parents or grandparents personal names, etc. The inherited name (this being the lastname in western cultures) may be compound (e.g. 'Fischer von Waldheim', 'da Selva', 'Silvano Morales'). Depending on culture, the inherited name is not necessarily the name of the parents nor common to a married couple. Therefore, 'family name' should be avoided even though used in vCard (vCard: N-Family).

Term Name abcd2:SpecimenUnit-AcquiredFrom-InheritedName
Term IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/SpecimenUnit-AcquiredFrom-InheritedName
Label InheritedName
Definition The inherited name of the person from whom the specimen was acquired. This may consist of family names, generational names, a clan name, parents or grandparents personal names, etc. The inherited name (this being the lastname in western cultures) may be compound (e.g. 'Fischer von Waldheim', 'da Selva', 'Silvano Morales'). Depending on culture, the inherited name is not necessarily the name of the parents nor common to a married couple. Therefore, 'family name' should be avoided even though used in vCard (vCard: N-Family).

Term Name abcd2:SpecimenUnit-PreparationAgent-InheritedName
Term IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/SpecimenUnit-PreparationAgent-InheritedName
Label InheritedName
Definition The inherited name of the person acting as or representing the specimen preparation agent. This may consist of family names, generational names, a clan name, parents or grandparents personal names, etc. The inherited name (this being the lastname in western cultures) may be compound (e.g. 'Fischer von Waldheim', 'da Selva', 'Silvano Morales'). Depending on culture, the inherited name is not necessarily the name of the parents nor common to a married couple. Therefore, 'family name' should be avoided even though used in vCard (vCard: N-Family).

Definition The personal name of the person acting as or representing the specimen preparation agent. The name given to the person as a personal name (the first or christian name in western cultures, including middle initials). The given name may contain several words. It is applicable only to people (vCard: N-Given + vCard: N-Middle).

Term Name abcd2:PreviousUnit-DateText
Term IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/PreviousUnit-DateText
Label DateText
Definition A text version (alphabetic mixed case and integer) of the date(s) during which the unit was held by a previous collection. This element is meant for use when the date is imprecise, ambiguous or not in a form that satisfies the standard structured date format. It can also be used when it is important to record the verbatim representation of the date or when dates to be recorded are not completely legible. For example the day and month may be decipherable but not the year; the use of this field will allow recording of partially interpreted information. <br/><br/>This field can be used to record generalised date ranges and irresolvable ambiguity such as different day/month order conventions (e.g. US/Europe) or to allow for multiple dates and periods. <br/><br/>In the rare instances of dates for periods before the year 0000, BC and similar dates can be recorded in this field.
Examples
  • 25 [?] 1925
  • 3/9/45 [ambiguous day month]
  • Spring 1912
  • Late 1800s
  • End of 19th Century
  • Mid 1978
  • Easter 1933
  • Post WW2
  • Before June 25, 2000
  • After June 25, 2000
XPath /DataSets/DataSet/Units/Unit/SpecimenUnit/History/PreviousUnits/PreviousUnit/Date/DateText
Parent PreviousUnit-Date
Belongs to Group SpecimenUnit
Required False
Repeatable False
Position within Parent 1
RDF Type rdf:Property
Modified 2005-09-09

Label TimeZone
Definition The time zone to which the time-of-day data for the specimen's history refer.<br/><br/>Timezone expressed in minutes in accordance with the seven property model for date/time attributes in XML schema ( http://www.w3.org/TR/2004/WD-xmlschema11-2-20040716/#theSevenPropertyModel). <br/><br/> An integer between -840 and 840 inclusive (+/- 14 hours).

Term Name abcd2:Gathering-DateTime-DateText
Term IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/Gathering-DateTime-DateText
Label DateText
Definition A text version (alphabetic mixed case and integer) of the date that the gathering event took place. This element is meant for use when the date is imprecise, ambiguous or not in a form that satisfies the standard structured date format. It can also be used when it is important to record the verbatim representation of the date or when dates to be recorded are not completely legible. For example the day and month may be decipherable but not the year; the use of this field will allow recording of partially interpreted information. <br/><br/>This field can be used to record generalised date ranges and irresolvable ambiguity such as different day/month order conventions (e.g. US/Europe) or to allow for multiple dates and periods. <br/><br/>In the rare instances of dates for periods before the year 0000, BC and similar dates can be recorded in this field.
Examples
  • 25 [?] 1925
  • 3/9/45 [ambiguous day month]
  • Spring 1912
  • Late 1800s
  • End of 19th Century
  • Mid 1978
  • Easter 1933
  • Post WW2
  • Before June 25, 2000
  • After June 25, 2000
XPath /DataSets/DataSet/Units/Unit/Gathering/DateTime/DateText
Parent Gathering-DateTime
Belongs to Group Gathering
Required False
Repeatable False
Position within Parent 1
RDF Type rdf:Property
Modified 2005-09-09
Term Version IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/version/Gathering-DateTime-DateText-2005-09-09
Term Name abcd2:Gathering-DateTime-TimeZone
Term IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/Gathering-DateTime-TimeZone
Label TimeZone
Definition The time zone to which the time-of-day data for the gathering event refer. <br/><br/>Timezone expressed in minutes in accordance with the seven property model for date/time attributes in XML schema ( http://www.w3.org/TR/2004/WD-xmlschema11-2-20040716/#theSevenPropertyModel). <br/><br/> An integer between -840 and 840 inclusive (+/- 14 hours).
Examples
  • +570
  • -300
XPath /DataSets/DataSet/Units/Unit/Gathering/DateTime/TimeZone
Parent Gathering-DateTime
Belongs to Group Gathering
Required False
Repeatable False
Position within Parent 2
RDF Type rdf:Property
Modified 2005-09-09
Term Version IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/version/Gathering-DateTime-TimeZone-2005-09-09
Term Name abcd2:Gathering-DateTime-ISODateTimeBegin
Term IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/Gathering-DateTime-ISODateTimeBegin
Label ISODateTimeBegin
Definition The exact date (and time) or beginning of a period representing the gathering event, expressed in a modified ISO/ANSI 8601 standard structured date format.
Usage The date format looks like this: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS with flexible precision.
Examples
  • 2005-04-10T17:34:56\n2005-04-10T17:34\n2005-04-10T17\n2005-04-10\n2005-04\n2005

Term Name abcd2:Gathering-DateTime-DayNumberBegin

Label DayNumberBegin
Definition The Julian day number (or sequential day) in the year for the exact date or for the first day of the gathering event. The year is given in ISO-Date-Time-Begin. <br/><br/>The content range is 1-365 for normal years, 366 for leap years. <br/><br/>Maps to Darwin Core 2: Julian Day.

Term Name abcd2:Gathering-DateTime-TimeOfDayBegin
Term IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/Gathering-DateTime-TimeOfDayBegin
Label TimeOfDayBegin
Definition The time of day in decimal hours from midnight local time for an exact point in time or for the beginning of the gathering event. <br/><br/>This field may apply to times of collecting where this is considered important. <br/><br/>Note that times are decimial hours: 13.5 represents 1:30 pm, not 1:05 pm, nor 1:50 pm. <br/><br/>Maps to Darwin Core 2: Time of Day.
Notes Note that time can also be expressed in the {{{ISODateTimeElement}}}.
Examples

  • 04.25

Term Name abcd2:GatheringAgent-Organisation-Abbreviation

Label Abbreviation
Definition Abbreviation representing the organisation acting as or associated with the gathering agent. For FAO/IPGRI multi-crop passport data (MCPD), this is the descriptor indicating the Institute collecting the sample (COLLCODE). If the holding institute has collected the material, this should be the same as the holding institute code (INSTCODE, in ABCD: SourceID). Restricted to 50 characters maximum length, including blanks (shorter recommended!). Label abbreviations are especially important when displaying information in a tabular format.

Term Name abcd2:GatheringAgent-InheritedName
Term IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/GatheringAgent-InheritedName
Label InheritedName
Definition The inherited name of the gathering agent. This may consist of family names, generational names, a clan name, parents or grandparents personal names, etc. The inherited name (this being the lastname in western cultures) may be compound (e.g. 'Fischer von Waldheim', 'da Selva', 'Silvano Morales'). Depending on culture, the inherited name is not necessarily the name of the parents nor common to a married couple. Therefore, 'family name' should be avoided even though used in vCard (vCard: N-Family).
XPath /DataSets/DataSet/Units/Unit/Gathering/Agents/GatheringAgent/Person/AtomisedName/InheritedName

Belongs to Group Gathering-Agent
Required True
Repeatable False

Label InheritedName
Definition The inherited name of the person to contact for information about the gathering project. This may consist of family names, generational names, a clan name, parents or grandparents personal names, etc. The inherited name (this being the lastname in western cultures) may be compound (e.g. 'Fischer von Waldheim', 'da Selva', 'Silvano Morales'). Depending on culture, the inherited name is not necessarily the name of the parents nor common to a married couple. Therefore, 'family name' should be avoided even though used in vCard (vCard: N-Family).

Term Name abcd2:Gathering-LocalityText
Term IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/Gathering-LocalityText
Label LocalityText
Definition The original gathering locality data as appearing on a label or in an original entry, as a text string. This field should be transcribed verbatim from the specimen label.<br/><br/>Location information below the country level that describes where the accession was collected. This might include the distance in kilometres and direction from the nearest town, village or map grid reference point. A FAO/IPGRI multi-crop passport descriptor (MCPD), description and examples taken from EURISCO descriptor list dated July 3, 2002.<br/><br/>Where possible, the language of the label locality should be indicated with the language attribute.<br/><br/>Editorial omissions for brevity, etc. should be indicated with an ellipsis (...) and interpreted or implied text should be included in square brackets [ ].
Examples
  • New Caledonia, below summit region of Mt Mou.
  • New South Wales, Central Tablelands 12 km SW of Armidale.
  • 7 km south of Curitiba in the state of Parana

Term Name abcd2:Gathering-Country
Term IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/Gathering-Country
Label Country
Definition Details about the gathering country, such as the representation of the country and its name. This is separate from {{{NamedArea}}} for compatibility reasons.<br/><br/>Maps to Darwin Core 2: Country through either {{{ISO2Letter}}} (future) or {{{CountryName}}} (current). Historical country names and water bodies outside the coastal zone can be entered under named area.<br/><br/>{{{CountryNameDerived}}} is provided for a country name that has been derived (e.g.from a system supplied dictionary) by library consultation or other independent research.<br/><br/>At least one of {{{CountryName}}} or {{{ISO2}}} or {{{ISO3}}} should be present but more are allowed. This should be the political country having jurisdiction over the collection site.
XPath /DataSets/DataSet/Units/Unit/Gathering/Country
Parent Gathering
Belongs to Group Gathering
Required False
Repeatable False
Position within Parent 1
RDF Type rdfs:Class
Modified 2005-09-09
Term Version IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/version/Gathering-Country-2005-09-09
Term Name abcd2:Gathering-Country-Name
Term IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/Gathering-Country-Name
Label Name
Definition The full name of the country or major region where the specimen was collected, or the observation made.<br/><br/>The use of this element is slightly ambiguous in that local practice might require either a verbatim quote from specimen labels, or standardisation by controlled vocabulary or lookup lists.<br/><br/>It is recommended that the spelling of the country be that which is recognised by the International Standards Organisation (ISO).<br/><br/>For cases where country names or boundaries have changed, it is recommended that new country names be enclosed in square brackets, after the old country name. The 2-letter ISO codes in the ISO Code for Country of Origin field assist with updating and cross referencing country names where boundaries change.<br/><br/>Separate fields for state/province and country are needed to adequately handle the situation with international collections.<br/><br/>If the name of the country where the plant was collected is unknown, then this field should contain the value 'UNKNOWN'. In this case, the ISO Code for Country of Origin field must have the entry 'XX' or 'XY'. All remaining 'location group' fields should be left unfilled.
Examples
  • Australia
  • Commonwealth of Australia
  • Iceland
  • Republic of Iceland
  • Samoa
  • Independent State of Samoa
XPath /DataSets/DataSet/Units/Unit/Gathering/Country/Name
Parent Gathering-Country
Belongs to Group Gathering
Required False
Repeatable False
Position within Parent 1
RDF Type rdf:Property
Modified 2005-09-09

Term Name abcd2:Gathering-Country-Name-@language

Definition The language of the text in the element carrying this attribute, according to RFC 3066.
Usage The value UND (undefined) should be used if the language cannot be set for some reason. Available at: http://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc3066.txt .\n

Term Name abcd2:Gathering-Country-NameDerived
Term IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/Gathering-Country-NameDerived
Label NameDerived
Definition The derived full name of the country or major region where the specimen was collected, or the observation made, interpreted in the light of contemporary geographical knowledge.<br/><br/>The use of this element is slightly ambiguous in that local practice might require either a verbatim quote from specimen labels, or standardisation by controlled vocabulary or lookup lists.<br/><br/>It is recommended that the spelling of the country should be that which is recognised by the International Standards Organisation (ISO).<br/><br/>The derived country name offers the opportunity to document the name under which a country is currently known, interpreted from an old or superceded name on the specimen label (e.g. Vanuatu for the New Hebrides, Sri Lanka for Ceylon, etc).<br/><br/>Separate fields for state/province and country are needed to adequately handle the situation with international collections.<br/><br/>If the name of the country where the plant was collected is unknown, then this field should contain the value 'UNKNOWN'. In this case, the ISO Code for Country of Origin field must have the entry 'XX', 'XY', 'XXX', or 'XXY'. All remaining 'location group' fields should be left unfilled.
Examples
  • Sri Lanka
  • Taiwan
  • Vanuatu
  • Papua New Guinea
  • Kiribati
  • East Timor

Parent Gathering-Country
Belongs to Group Gathering
Required False
Repeatable False

RDF Type rdf:Property
Modified 2005-09-09

Term Name abcd2:Gathering-Country-ISO3166Code
Term IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/Gathering-Country-ISO3166Code
Label ISO3166Code
Definition The 2-, 3-, or 4-letter code for the representation of the name of the gathering country using the codes assigned by the International Standards Organisation (ISO).<br/><br/>This field should contain a valid entry as defined by the International Standards Organisation (ISO Standard 3166-1), with the following exception: The 'XXX' or 'XX' code should be used when no country of origin information is provided. The 'XXY' or 'XY' code should be used for non-specific collecting localities, e.g. Africa, SouthEast Asia.
Notes Note: The letter code identifies a country name, NOT a physical territory. For the latter, there is a ISO 3166 numerical code. For exemple, when Germany reunified, it kept DE/DEU but changed from 280 to 276, while when Southern Rhodesia was renamed Zimbabwe it stayed 716 but changed from RH/RHO to ZW/ZWE.<br/><br/>See comments under Country.
Examples
  • AU
  • ES
  • FR
  • PG
  • US
  • AUS
  • ESP
  • FRA
  • USA
  • DDDE

Term Name abcd2:Gathering-PointRadiusSpatialFit
Term IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/Gathering-PointRadiusSpatialFit
Label PointRadiusSpatialFit
Definition DwC Geospatial Extension v. 1.4: ] A measure of how well the circle defined by the coordinates and uncertainty match the original spatial representation, as a ratio of the area of the circle to the area of the original spatial representation. Legal values are 0, greater than or equal to 1, or undefined. A value of 1 is an exact match or 100% overlap. A value of 0 should be used if the given georeference does not completely contain the original representation. The PointRadiusSpatialFit is undefined if the original representation is a point without uncertainty and the given georeference is not that same point (without uncertainty). If both the original and the given georeference are the same point, the PointRadiusSpatialFit is 1. Detailed explanations with graphical examples can be found in the Guide to Best Practices for Georeferencing (Chapman and Wieczorek, eds. 2006).

Required False

Term IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/Gathering-Altitude
Label Altitude
Definition The altitude of the gathering site land or floor level, given as distance above (positive) or below mean sea level. Although the altitude could be covered by the generic element for site measurements, the separate altitude element is preserved for the sake of clarity.
Notes Note the difference from the {{{Height}}} and {{{Depth}}} elements, which are measured relative to a local surface.

Belongs to Group Gathering-MeasurementOrFact
Required False
Repeatable False

Term Name abcd2:Gathering-Depth

Term Name abcd2:Synecology
Term IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/Synecology
Label Synecology
Definition The relationship of the unit gathered with other taxa at the gathering site.
Notes Note that this relationship can be recorded as a feature of the location (e.g. a syntaxon, or certain species known to grow together at the site). It can also be used to record an observed relationship (e.g. caterpillar and observed food plant, parasite and host etc.), but this would be better expressed as a unit association.

Label GenusOrMonomial
Definition One of the following, representing the genus, or higher taxon name, that is part of the identification for the associated taxon for the unit.<br/><br/>A generic name as a botanical scientific name or as part of it. <br/><br/>A generic name under one of the established nomenclatural codes <br/><br/>A manuscript name<br/><br/>An intergeneric hybrid name under the ICBN, without the leading multiplication sign, <br/><br/>The name of an intergeneric graft hybrid or graft chimaera, published under the Cultivated Code.<br/><br/>Rules: <br/><br/>1. First letter capitalised. <br/><br/>2. No spaces included.
Notes Generic names are essentially the same under the different codes; however, to avoid having to place the essential parts of a name on different levels of the hierarchy, all name elements recognized under a specific code are listed in the respective section.

Term Name abcd2:Gathering-FootprintSpatialFit
Term IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/Gathering-FootprintSpatialFit
Label FootprintSpatialFit
Definition [DwC Geospacial Extension Schema v. 0.3] A measure of how well the geometry expressed in the footprint match the original spatial representation, as a ratio of the area of the footprint given to the area of the original spatial representation. Legal values are 0, greater than or equal to 1, or undefined. A value of 1 is an exact match or 100% overlap. A value of 0 should be used if the given georeference does not completely contain the original representation. The FootprintSpatialFit is undefined if the original representation is a point without uncertainty and the given georeference is not that same point (without uncertainty). If both the original and the given georeference are the same point, the FootprintSpatialFit is 1. Detailed explanations with graphical examples can be found in the Guide to Best Practices for Georeferencing (Chapman and Wieczorek, eds. 2006)
XPath /DataSets/DataSet/Units/Unit/Gathering/FootprintSpatialFit
Parent Gathering
Belongs to Group Gathering

Modified 2006-10-09

Term Name abcd2:CollectorsFieldNumber
Term IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/CollectorsFieldNumber
Label CollectorsFieldNumber
Definition The original number assigned to the unit by the collector or observer. The entire desiganation is normally composed of the name or initials of the collector(s) followed by a number. This number is essential for identifying duplicates held in different collections. <br/><br/>This identifier should be added to the entry (for collectors) under {{{Gathering/GatheringAgents/../Person}}}, if such an entry exists. However, the collector (or collector abbreviation) and number can also be given in a single field (e.g. FAO/IPGRI multi-crop passport descriptor (MCPD), described in the EURISCO descriptor list dated July 3, 2002). In that case, the entire string may be entered here.

Label InheritedName
Definition The inherited name of the unit sequencing agent. This may consist of family names, generational names, a clan name, parents or grandparents personal names, etc. The inherited name (this being the lastname in western cultures) may be compound (e.g. 'Fischer von Waldheim', 'da Selva', 'Silvano Morales'). Depending on culture, the inherited name is not necessarily the name of the parents nor common to a married couple. Therefore, 'family name' should be avoided even though used in vCard (vCard: N-Family).

Term Name abcd2:UnitExtension
Term IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/UnitExtension
Label UnitExtension
Definition The extension is temporary and serves only to accommodate urgent inter-version additions to the unit-object schema [in the future to the the various schemas/objects used in ABCD]. <br/><br/>For example, if a specific community (e.g. culture collections) discover that there are elements missing in the current version of ABCD (as they did for 1.2), they communicate that to the group responsible for schema development, who will discuss whether these elements are already accommodated in the schema, if they are not and if they can and should be generalized, and where they should end up in the schema. IF the culture collection community needs to move rapidly (e.g. due to project pressures), they can add these elements to the current version as an extension schema under a structure that follows SDD's CustomExtensions element (CustomExtensions-CustomExtension-Any ##other). In future modular versions of ABCD, such a structure should exist in the root of every object/schema.
XPath /DataSets/DataSet/Units/Unit/UnitExtension
Parent Unit
Belongs to Group Unit
Required False
Repeatable False
Position within Parent 1
RDF Type rdfs:Class
Modified 2005-09-09
Term Version IRI http://rs.tdwg.org/abcd2/terms/version/UnitExtension-2005-09-09
